title: Choose the visual world for 77prophets.patpadgett.com
question: The roll assigned The Outlaw Broadside. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Outlaw Broadside
options.lineage: 19th-century American letterpress job printing: wanted bills and revival proclamations
options.thesis: Every release is a proclamation nailed to the post: wood type, black stock, gold and bone ink.
options.viewport: One full-bleed bill. 77PROPHETS in wood type across the whole measure; the outlet line (Spotify, YouTube, Suno, Apple) set as a rule-bound line of type directly under it; the claymation promo as a tipped-in portrait plate on the right with the gold seal as its play stamp; the newest release as the lead notice on the left with its own play and its Suno style tag.
options.risk: Reads as costume if the type is set timidly or the distress is sprayed on uniformly; every ink effect must belong to a specific object.

raised.raise: Distress is authored per object: each plate gets its own ink squash and misregistration offset; no uniform grain overlay anywhere.
The bill's deckled paper edge is generated SVG geometry that regenerates at every width.
Each track row carries a spot tint sampled from its own cover.
The one motion moment runs on a beat, not a curve: the seal press-stamps in stepped frames.
Every rule and column snaps to one baseline grid at whole-pixel positions.
Covers emerge in one continuous reveal down the bill, never scattered fades.

regions.label: outlet line: Spotify · YouTube · Suno · Apple
lead notice: newest release + play + style tag
tipped-in promo plate (portrait video) + seal stamp

options.label: The Firmament Chart
options.lineage: Gleason's 1892 azimuthal world map and engraved celestial charts
options.thesis: The catalog plotted as named stars beneath the dome he sings about.
options.viewport: The engraved dome fills the first screen; releases sit as named stars along the rings; the play control is the zenith; outlets ring the horizon.
options.risk: The literal reading of his creed and the card a reader could predict; a map-first page can also bury the play button under decoration.

options.label: Hand-Processed 16mm
options.lineage: hand-processed film with scratches, uneven chemistry, and light leaks
options.thesis: The catalog runs as one scratched strip; each release is a frame, the promo video the projected reel.
options.viewport: A vertical strip of frames down the page, edge codes in the margin, the newest release in the active, leaked frame.
options.case: Fuses cleanly (he is a former media producer with a video channel; frames map to releases) but his listeners identify with outlaw Americana, not arthouse film.
options.risk: Reads as an Instagram filter when the artifacts are not tied to specific frames.

options.label: Rubber-Hose Cel
options.thesis: The project as a 1930s cartoon reel with iris wipes between gags.
options.viewport: An oval iris opens on a bouncing scene; controls squash when pressed.
options.case: Contradicts every cover in the catalog and his audience does not identify with Fleischer-era cartoons.
options.kept: Motion on a beat, not a curve.
options.risk: Whimsy against a sincere, dark catalog.

options.label: Village Coffeehouse Identity
options.lineage: nineties earthy corporate identity: woodcut sun over torn kraft
options.thesis: Releases as stations on a friendly kraft-paper map.
options.viewport: A woodcut mark over torn paper; warm humanist caps; sections stamped as you move.
options.case: Terracotta and olive contradict the gold-on-black seal, and 'friendly organic' is the opposite of a prophet's register.
options.kept: Torn edges generated responsively, never a fixed image.

options.label: Sleeping City Fold
options.thesis: Neighborhoods fold into blankets; each district dreams its own weather.
options.viewport: A folded night city with stitched district names.
options.case: Listeners do not identify with a dreaming city, and a catalog gains no clarity from map folds.
options.kept: Each district its own hue: per-track tint from its cover.
options.risk: Pure surrealism with no handle on the music.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.lineage: early one-bit desktop, dithered grays and marching ants
options.thesis: The catalog as overlapping windows on a black-and-white desktop.
options.viewport: Windows tile a desktop; the newest release is the front window.
options.case: Dithering destroys the cinematic covers that carry this project, and the audience has no bond with 1984 desktops.
options.kept: Whole-pixel discipline: one strict baseline grid.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight Bay
options.thesis: Covers emerge in the developer tray as you scroll.
options.viewport: Amber-washed stations in order; the newest print surfacing in the tray.
options.case: The compose/expose/develop topology has no honest mapping onto a song catalog; identification is with photographers, not his listeners.
options.kept: One continuous emergence for the reveal.
options.risk: Amber wash flattens every cover to the same tone.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark band site: big name, Spotify button, cover grid, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Name and tagline over a hero image, two buttons, a grid of covers below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other artist page, by design.
